name: Chromosome Y Microdeletion Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Academy of Andrology Guidelines for Y Chromosome Microdeletion

criteria.description: Presence of azoospermia or severe oligospermia on semen analysis
Detection of microdeletions in the AZF (azoospermia factor) regions of the Y chromosome by PCR or FISH
Clinical features such as testicular atrophy or infertility with normal secondary sexual characteristics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of Y chromosome microdeletion in AZF regions combined with azoospermia or severe oligospermia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires molecular confirmation; clinical features alone are insufficient.

laboratory: Semen analysis showing azoospermia or severe oligospermia
Normal or mildly decreased testosterone levels
imaging: Testicular ultrasound showing reduced testicular volume and heterogeneous echotexture

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated LH and FSH with low testosterone
Low or normal FSH and LH levels

redFlags: Complete azoospermia in a male with normal secondary sexual characteristics
Testicular atrophy without other endocrine abnormalities
Family history of male infertility or Y chromosome microdeletions
references: Krausz C, Hoefsloot L, Simoni M, Tüttelmann F. EAA/EMQN best practice guidelines for molecular diagnosis of Y-chromosomal microdeletions: state-of-the-art 2013. Andrology. 2014 Jan;2(1):5-19.
Foresta C, Ferlin A. Y chromosome microdeletions and alterations of spermatogenesis. Endocrine. 2004 Jun;23(2-3):197-204.
